product.name: Microsoft Graph (authorized through the Microsoft identity platform / Microsoft Entra ID)

source.quote: Microsoft Graph is a protected API gateway for accessing data in Microsoft cloud services like Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365.

oauthAppCreation.where: Microsoft Entra admin center: Entra ID > App registrations > New registration

source.quote: Browse to Entra ID > App registrations and select New registration.

reviewGate.trigger: No approval queue exists for Graph delegated permissions. Publisher verification (automated, no cost) gates user consent for multitenant apps in other tenants; admin consent gates high-privilege permissions; AppSource and Microsoft 365 App Certification are optional.

source.quote: users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified

approvalWait.stated: Publisher verification: minutes once the prerequisites (a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account) are met. Time to verify that partner account is not stated.

source.quote: Developers who have already met these requirements can be verified in minutes.

testBeforeApproval.how: Register a single-tenant app and sign in with users in your own tenant; no review is involved

source.quote: For single-tenant apps for use only by users (or guests) in your tenant.
the app requests the User.Read and Mail.Read Microsoft Graph permissions, which allow the app to read the profile and mail of the signed-in user respectively.
the app requests the User.Read and Mail.Read Microsoft Graph permissions, which allow the app to read the profile and mail of the signed-in user respectively.
The offline_access permission is a standard OIDC scope that's requested so that the app can get a refresh token.
The Calendars.Read delegated permission is available for consent in personal Microsoft accounts.

blockers.summary: Application permissions and many high-privilege delegated permissions need an administrator to grant consent

source.quote: application permissions and many high-privilege delegated permissions can only be consented to by an administrator

blockers.summary: Users in other tenants cannot consent to most new multitenant apps that lack publisher verification

source.quote: users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified

blockers.summary: An Azure account with at least the Application Developer role and a tenant are needed to register an app

source.quote: The Azure account must be at least an Application Developer

blockers.summary: Tenant administrators can disable user consent, so users are not prompted and cannot use the app

source.quote: If user consent is disabled, or users aren't allowed to consent for the requested permissions, they aren't prompted for consent.

avoidProducts.name: Azure AD B2C
avoidProducts.why: Customer identity service with its own app registrations; not the way an agent calls Microsoft Graph for a user
avoidProducts.evidence: Stored microsoft guide cited a B2C client credentials page in 9 of 24 claims (08b, case 3)

avoidProducts.name: Azure DevOps OAuth
avoidProducts.why: Azure DevOps has its own OAuth scopes (such as user_impersonation); they are not Microsoft Graph permissions
avoidProducts.evidence: Baseline run 2026-10-29: the Microsoft guide cites devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/new-azure-devops-scopes-now-available-for-microsoft-identity-oauth-delegated-flow-apps for the scope user_impersonation (apps/api/evals/diagnosis.md, section 7)

notes: Microsoft has no review queue. required_to_scale is primary because unverified multitenant apps hit user-consent limits in other tenants; none is the one accepted alternate. Approved by the owner on 2026-10-29.
The Azure DevOps avoidProducts entry was added after the first baseline run. It was not in the golden set approved on 2026-10-29.
The wait is minutes for publisher verification only; the partner-account verification time is not stated, so confidence is low.
